page: Amazon Web Services c7i.48xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 vCPUs and 96 physical cores from an Intel Xeon 8488C processor operating at 3.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but provides a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in multi-core operations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU score, and PassMark CPU extended instructions all rank in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only cached and uncached large-block operations scoring in the top 10%, while write operations rank in the top 25%. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU and bzip3 decompression single-threaded benchmarks falling into the average tier.

The hardware profile presents specific architectural tradeoffs. While multi-threaded capabilities, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput are in the top 10%, the lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage. The instance is optimized for compute-heavy workloads such as ray tracing, image processing, database operations, and software compilation, which leverage the advanced vector and matrix extensions (AVX-512 and AMX) built into the Intel Xeon processor.
